consent.title: Google Takeout Study
consent.ethics: Ethical approval: this study is awaiting review by the University of Surrey's ethics committee. Its approval reference will be shown here once approval is granted.
consent.intro: You are about to start the process of donating data from your Google Takeout export to our study. We ask for your recent screen time (YouTube viewing times, and your Google Play Movies & TV watchlist and viewing history) and health and activity data (Google Fit, Google Health and Google Play Games playtime). For Google Fit this includes the individual timestamped samples of heart rate, steps, distance, calories, activity type and sleep stages, not only daily totals, and we do not read or collect your location. The data will be used for academic research on screen time, physical activity and wellbeing.
consent.process: We will walk you through this process step by step. During this process no data is stored or sent to a server. Only data from the last 6 months is kept; anything older is removed automatically on your own computer. YouTube video titles, channels, links and search terms are never read into the donation, only when you watched or searched. You can also delete rows before donating. Data will only be donated and stored when you click the button "Yes, donate" on the page that shows your data.

dataScope.title: What we ask for, and what is actually read
dataScope.intro: Your Google Takeout download may contain data from the services below. This tool reads only the data listed for each one, on your own computer:

services.name: Fit
services.read: your daily activity totals (steps, distance, calories, active and heart minutes), your recorded workouts, and the individual timestamped samples of heart rate, steps, distance, calories, activity type and sleep stages.
services.notRead: your location and GPS tracks, and every other kind of Fit data (for example weight, height or sensor readings).

services.name: Google Health (or Fitbit)
services.read: daily activity totals (steps, distance, calories, active minutes), heart-rate summaries and resting heart rate, heart-rate variability, blood-oxygen and respiratory-rate summaries, your sleep (nights, stages and score) and your exercise sessions.
services.notRead: your profile and account details, paired devices, location and GPS, weather, nutrition, weight, menstrual and ECG data, and messages.

services.name: Google Play Games Services
services.read: which games you played and when: daily playtime per game, and the first and last time each game was played.
services.notRead: your player profile and picture, scores, achievements and saved game data.

services.name: Google Play Movies & TV
services.read: your watchlist and your viewing history, if your download has one: the titles and the dates and times you saved or watched them.
services.notRead: your purchases, rentals, ratings and every other file in that folder. None of it is used or donated.

services.name: YouTube and YouTube Music
services.read: only when you watched or searched: dates and times, how many videos you watched, music tracks you played and searches you made, and estimated viewing sessions.
services.notRead: video titles, channel names, links and search text are not kept in the donation, and your subscriptions, playlists, comments and uploads are not read.

dataScope.subsetNote: For every service above, only the data listed under "Read" is used; everything else in those folders is ignored.
dataScope.otherServices: Your export may contain other services as well. This tool does not read them: they are never opened, and nothing from them is donated.

sections.title: Who is running this study
paragraphs: This study is run by researchers at the University of Surrey: Dr Tamas Foldes (Surrey Sleep Research Centre), Dr Zsofia Zavecz and Dr Oscar Ferrante (School of Psychology). The University of Surrey is the data controller, which means it is responsible for your data.
For questions, or to withdraw your donation, email t.foldes@surrey.ac.uk.

sections.title: What we store
paragraphs: When you click "Yes, donate", we store:
items: the data you choose to donate on the review page, without any rows or data types you removed;
your submission ID (a random 16-digit number shown after you donate) and the date and time of your donation;

two technical details that your browser sends to every website: a scrambled code made from your IP address (the address itself is not stored), and your browser's identification string (its name, version and operating system). These are used only to block repeated or automated submissions.

sections.title: Storage, access and retention
paragraphs: We do not collect your name, email address or Google account details.
Your donation is encrypted as soon as it reaches our server and is stored on servers managed by the University of Surrey. Only the research team named above holds the key that can decrypt it.

Before your donation is sent, Cloudflare, a security service, checks that you are a person and not an automated program. Cloudflare receives your IP address for this check. It is not used for advertising or analytics.
Your data will be kept for 10 years after the study ends and then deleted.

sections.title: How your data is used and shared
paragraphs: Your donation is pseudonymised, not anonymous. It contains no name or account details, but detailed records with exact times (for example your heart rate, sleep and viewing times) could in principle be linked to you by someone who already knows a lot about you. For that reason:
items: the individual records you donate stay with the University of Surrey research team and are not published or shared with anyone else;
publications and presentations contain only aggregate results, such as averages across many participants, from which no individual can be identified.

sections.title: Your rights and how to withdraw
paragraphs: Taking part is voluntary. You can stop at any point before you click "Yes, donate", and nothing will be sent.

After donating, you can withdraw within 1 month: email t.foldes@surrey.ac.uk with your submission ID and we will delete your donation. Keep the ID safe. We do not know who you are, so the ID is the only way to find your donation. After 1 month your data may already be part of our analyses, and it can no longer be withdrawn.

The University of Surrey processes your data under UK data protection law (UK GDPR) as a task in the public interest (Article 6(1)(e)). Health data, such as heart rate and sleep, is a special category of personal data, so it is processed for scientific research purposes (Article 9(2)(j)) with safeguards, including encryption and pseudonymisation. Research ethics also requires your explicit consent, which is why we ask for it below.

The University's information governance page explains your data protection rights and how to contact its Data Protection Officer. You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk).

agreementPoints: you explicitly and voluntarily agree to donate the data shown on the review page, including health data such as heart rate, sleep and activity, for this research.
you understand that your donation is pseudonymised, not anonymous, that the individual records stay with the research team, and that only aggregate results will be published.
you understand that you can withdraw your donation within 1 month by emailing your submission ID to t.foldes@surrey.ac.uk, and not after that.
consent.agreementCheckbox: I have read and agree with the above terms.

upload.title: Upload File
upload.intro: Please export your data from Google Takeout (takeout.google.com). Select "Fit", "Google Health" or "Fitbit" (if you have them), "Google Play Games Services" and "YouTube and YouTube Music" (under its options, include "history"), then download the export. Also select "Google Play Movies & TV" if you have it. Any other service in the download is ignored. Google may split it into several .zip files: choose all of them at once.
upload.dropHint: Or drag and drop the .zip files, or the folder that contains them, here. You can add files in several steps.
upload.processing: Processing your file... This may take a few moments for large exports.
upload.incorrectFile: The uploaded files might be incorrect, corrupted, or contain no recent data from the supported Google services.
upload.possibleIssues: We were unable to find any usable data from the last 6 months in the uploaded files. This could mean:
issuePoints: The files are not a Google Takeout export
The export did not include Fit, Google Health, Google Play Games Services, Google Play Movies & TV or YouTube history
You did not select every .zip part of a split export
All of the data in the export is older than 6 months
The YouTube history is not in English (other languages are not supported yet)
The files are corrupted or incomplete
upload.checkFile: Please check that you selected all the .zip files of your Google Takeout export or contact the researchers for assistance.
upload.note: Note: The process to extract the correct data from the files is done on your own computer. No data is stored or sent yet. Extraction may take a while for large exports.

filter.intro: Determine whether you would like to donate the data below. Carefully check the data and adjust when required. You can filter by date range, exclude specific activity types or data streams, and delete specific rows. With your donation you contribute to the previously described research. Thank you in advance.
filter.excludeLabel: Exclude activity types or data streams
filter.excludePlaceholder: Select activity types or data streams to remove
filter.donationPrompt: Do you want to donate the above data?
filter.note: Note: Sending the data may take several seconds depending on the data size.
filter.windowNotice: Only data from the last {months} months is kept. {count} rows from before then (or without a readable date) were removed automatically on your computer and will not be donated.

thankyou.title: Thank You!
thankyou.successMessage: Your data has been successfully submitted. Thank you for your contribution!
thankyou.saveId: Please save this ID. We do not know who you are, so it is the only way to find your donation. To withdraw within 1 month of today, email this ID to t.foldes@surrey.ac.uk.
thankyou.declineMessage: Thank you for your time. Your decision has been recorded and no data has been shared.
